issues.description: Class UniqueTable: the template dd.py declares the internal storage field as a private attribute '__table' but all methods (lookup, clear, __init__) use 'self.table'. The solution dd.py uses a public field named 'table' and the methods reference 'self.table'. Because the problem statement explicitly instructs students not to modify dd.py, this naming mismatch in the template will cause AttributeError at runtime (methods expect 'table' but only '__table' is defined) and will confuse students who rely on the provided dd.py. Files involved: template/dd.py (declaration of '__table' and method bodies referencing 'self.table'), solution/dd.py (declaration and use of 'table'), and problem_statement.md (instructions that dd.py should not need modification).
issues.suggestedFix: Make the internal storage attribute name consistent in the template dd.py. Replace the private declaration '__table: dict[int, DDNode]' with 'table: dict[int, DDNode]' and set 'self.table = {}' in __init__, or alternatively change all method references to use the declared private name (self.__table). Prefer the solution's public name 'table' so template and solution match and students do not need to modify dd.py.
